'''Dagmar Elisabeth Schipanski''' ({{Née|'''Eichhorn'''}}; 3 September 1943 – 7 September 2022) was a German [[physicist]], academic, and politician from [[Thuringia]]. Although best known for her [[1999 German presidential election|1999 nomination]] as [[President of Germany]] by the conservative [[Christian Democratic Union of Germany|Christian Democratic Union]] (CDU) and its sister party, the [[Christian Social Union of Bavaria]] (CSU), Schipanski held a variety of political and academic roles during her four-decade-long career and was awarded numerous honors, most notably the [[Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany]] in 1996.<ref name="Oelze 2015" />

== Early life ==
Schipanski was born on 3 September 1943 in [[Sättelstädt]], Thuringia, which later became a part of the [[German Democratic Republic]].<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Wissenschaft idw 2022">{{cite web | title=TU Ilmenau trauert um ihre ehemalige Rektorin Prof. Dagmar Schipanski | website=Nachrichten aus der Wissenschaft, idw | date=9 September 2022 | url=https://nachrichten.idw-online.de/2022/09/09/tu-ilmenau-trauert-um-ihre-ehemalige-rektorin-prof-dagmar-schipanski | language=de | access-date=10 September 2022}}</ref> Her mother was a teacher, and her father was a pastor, who died in World War II.<ref name="GmbH">{{cite web | title=Dagmar Schipanski | website=Munzinger Biographie | url=https://www.munzinger.de/search/portrait/Dagmar+Schipanski/0/21742.html | language=de | access-date=10 September 2022}}</ref><ref name="Bundesstiftung zur Aufarbeitung der SED-Diktatur">{{cite web | title=Schipanski, Dagmar | website=Bundesstiftung zur Aufarbeitung der SED-Diktatur | url=https://www.bundesstiftung-aufarbeitung.de/de/recherche/kataloge-datenbanken/biographische-datenbanken/dagmar-schipanski | language=de | access-date=10 September 2022}}</ref> After graduating from high school in 1962,<ref name="Oelze 2015">{{cite web | last=Oelze | first=Dorothea | title=Dagmar Schipanski | website=Geschichte der CDU | date=26 October 2015 | url=https://www.kas.de/en/web/geschichte-der-cdu/biogram-detail/-/content/dagmar-schipanski-v1 | access-date=10 September 2022}}</ref> she became a student of [[applied physics]] at the [[Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg|Technical University of Magdeburg]].<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Wissenschaft idw 2022" /> In 1967, Schipanski began her career as an engineer, followed by a period of working as an assistant at [[TU Ilmenau]]. After earning her doctorate in 1976,<ref name="Oelze 2015" /> Schipanski began her academic career as a lecturer in [[Ilmenau]] and, starting in 1990, as a professor. She served as [[Dean (academia)|Dean]] of the Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology at TU Ilmenau from 1992 to 1993 and as [[Rector (academia)|Rector]] of TU Ilmenau from 1995 to 1996.<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Wissenschaft idw 2022" />

From 1996 to 1998, Schipanski served as chair of the [[German Council of Science and Humanities]], an advisory body that makes recommendations on the development of science and research to both the federal government and the state governments of Germany.<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Wissenschaft idw 2022" /> She was elected to the [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|Leopoldina]],<ref name="Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften Leopoldina 2021">{{cite web | title=Mitglieder | website=Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften Leopoldina | date=25 September 2021 | url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/dagmar-schipanski/ | language=de | access-date=10 September 2022}}</ref><ref name="Bundesstiftung zur Aufarbeitung der SED-Diktatur" /> the national academy of Germany, in 1998, and served as a member of the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Mitgliederverzeichnis: Dagmar Schipanski|publisher=Academia Europaea|url=http://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Schipanski_Dagmar|access-date=17 June 2017}}</ref>

== Political career ==
Despite not being a member of either party, Schipanski was nominated by the CDU and the CSU to be their candidate in the 1999 Presidential election.<ref name="Schmollack 2022">{{cite news | last=Schmollack | first=Simone | title=Dagmar Schipanski ist tot: Mit Mut zum Risiko | newspaper=Die Tageszeitung: Taz | date=9 September 2022 | url=https://taz.de/!5881000/ | language=de | access-date=10 September 2022}}</ref> Schipanski lost the election to the former [[Minister-President of North Rhine-Westphalia|minister-president of North Rhine-Westphalia]], [[Johannes Rau]], a member of the [[Social Democratic Party of Germany|Social Democratic Party]], receiving 572 votes to Rau's 690 on the second ballot.<ref name="Schmollack 2022" /><ref name="Wahlergebnisse">{{cite web | title=Bundespräsidentenwahlen | website=Wahlergebnisse | url=https://www.wahlen-in-deutschland.de/bBPW.htm | language=de | access-date=10 September 2022}}</ref>

After her defeat, Schipanski remained active in politics and was appointed Minister of Science, Research, and the Arts in the cabinet of the [[Minister-President of Thuringia|minister-president of Thuringa]], [[Bernhard Vogel]], later that year.<ref name="Schmollack 2022" /> Schipanski would later join the CDU in 1999 and would remain in her ministerial position until 2004 when she was elected to the [[Landtag of Thuringia]] and became [[President of the Landtag of Thuringia|President of the Landtag]].<ref name="Schmollack 2022" /> Schipanski lost her position in the Landtag as a result of the [[2009 Thuringian state election|2009 state election]].<ref name="Schmollack 2022" />

== Personal life ==
Schipanski, a [[Protestant]], was married and had three children.<ref name="Oelze 2015" /> One of her children, [[Tankred Schipanski|Tankred]], was a member of the [[Bundestag]] from 2009<ref name="Deutscher Bundestag">{{cite web | title=Tankred Schipanski | website=Deutscher Bundestag | url=https://www.bundestag.de/webarchiv/abgeordnete/biografien19/S/schipanski_tankred-523278 | language=de | access-date=10 September 2022}}</ref> until
2021.


Schipanski died on 7 September 2022 at the age of 79, after a short, serious illness.<ref name="tagesschau-obit">{{cite news |title=CDU-Politikerin Dagmar Schipanski ist tot |url=https://www.tagesschau.de/inland/dagmar-schipanski-103.html |access-date=9 September 2022 |work=.de |date=9 September 2022 |language=de}}</ref><ref name="zdf-obit">{{cite news |title=CDU-Politikerin: Dagmar Schipanski stirbt mit 79 Jahren |url=https://www.zdf.de/nachrichten/panorama/dagmar-schipanski-tot-cdu-100.html |access-date=9 September 2022 |work=www.zdf.de |date=9 September 2022 |language=de}}</ref>

== Memberships ==
Since 1998, Schipanski has been a member of the board of directors of the [[Mitteldeutscher Rundfunk|MDR]]. From 2001 to 2007, she served as a member of the [[UNESCO]] World Commission on the Ethics of Scientific Knowledge and Technology.<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Wissenschaft idw 2022" /> From 2000 to 2009, Schipanski served as President of the [[German Cancer Aid]]. She has served as a member of the board of trustees of the [[Deutsche Stiftung Denkmalschutz|German Foundation for Monument Protection]] since 2000, as chair of the board of the [[Lennart Bernadotte]] Foundation since 2003,<ref name="Oelze 2015" /> and, since 2005, as the chair of the board of trustees of the [[Fraunhofer Society|Fraunhofer Institute for Digital Media Technology]].<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Wissenschaft idw 2022" />

Schipanski was an ambassador for the [[New Social Market Economy initiative]]{{cn|date=September 2023}} and has served as a member of the Presidium of the Oskar Patzelt Foundation.<ref name="GmbH 2016">{{cite web | title=Prof. Dagmar Schipanski wird Präsidiumsmitglied der Oskar-Patzelt-Stiftung | website=www.pt-magazin.de | date=27 April 2016 | url=https://www.pt-magazin.de/de/wirtschaft/unternehmen/prof-dagmar-schipanski-wird-pr%C3%A4sidiumsmitglied-der_vd.html?s=CSo7ZOajRPtP0iVX6zh | language=de | access-date=10 September 2022}}</ref> She temporarily served as a member of the board of trustees of the [[Körber Foundation]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dagmar-schipanski.de/|title=Fr. Prof. Dr.-Ing. habil. Dagmar Schipanski|website=www.dagmar-schipanski.de}}</ref> before leaving her post due to pressure from anti-tobacco activists.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.taz.de/!569035/|title=Schipanski raucht nicht|date=29 July 2005|pages=22|via=www.taz.de|newspaper=Die Tageszeitung: Taz}}</ref> Since 2008, Schipanski has served as a member of the board of trustees of the International Martin Luther Foundation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.luther-stiftung.org/index.php?id=67&L=-1|title=Internationale Martin Luther Stiftung|website=www.luther-stiftung.org|access-date=8 November 2017|archive-date=11 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171011072336/http://www.luther-stiftung.org/index.php?id=67&L=-1|url-status=dead}}</ref>
